findings.evidence: TiDB collects FK-check lock keys into TxnCtx as *shared* for pessimistic txns (`pkg/executor/foreign_key.go:256-263`, `TransactionContext.AddUnchangedKeyForLock(k, true)`), and when the sysvar is ON it locks them in a second phase using `newLockCtx(..., shared=true)` / `txn.LockKeys` (`pkg/executor/adapter.go:1254-1277`). The client-go version pinned by this commit (`go.mod:127` => `github.com/tikv/client-go/v2 v2.0.8-0.20260209125252-1fd09ba3ef10`) explicitly rejects shared→exclusive lock upgrades: `.../txnkv/transaction/txn.go:1460` returns `"upgrading a shared lock to an exclusive lock is not supported"` (also asserted by `.../txnkv/transaction/txn_test.go:207-235`).
findings.fix: Document and gate the limitation (warn/forbid enabling when workloads may later write referenced rows), or implement true shared→exclusive lock upgrade support in TiKV/client-go. A TiDB-side workaround would require a safe upgrade path (e.g. pessimistic-rollback shared lock + re-lock exclusive with retry), which needs careful correctness/atomicity design.
findings.impact: Enabling `tidb_foreign_key_check_in_shared_lock` (session or global) can introduce user-visible errors in valid multi-statement pessimistic transactions, e.g. inserting/updating child rows (locking parent rows shared) and later updating/deleting the same parent rows in the same txn. This diverges from MySQL/InnoDB lock/transaction semantics and can break workloads that toggle or globally enable the feature for concurrency.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master`: `go.mod` at `upstream/master` pins `github.com/tikv/client-go/v2 v2.0.8-0.20260316081220-602cdf086c43`, and that version’s `txnkv/transaction/txn.go` still contains the same `upgrading a shared lock...is not supported` error.
findings.verify: Repro SQL: `BEGIN PESSIMISTIC; SET @@tidb_foreign_key_check_in_shared_lock=ON; INSERT INTO child VALUES (..., parent_id); UPDATE parent SET ... WHERE id=parent_id;` — expect either success (if upgrade supported) or a deterministic/clearly documented error. Add a RealTiKV regression test covering this pattern.
findings.what: With `tidb_foreign_key_check_in_shared_lock=ON`, FK checks acquire shared pessimistic locks on referenced keys; later statements in the same pessimistic transaction that need exclusive locks on those keys can fail because shared→exclusive lock upgrade is explicitly unsupported in client-go.

subject: *: implement shared lock for foreign key (#65752)
summary: Adds opt-in shared pessimistic locking for FK checks in pessimistic DML (two-phase xlock→slock) and updates coprocessor lock resolution for `SharedLockInfos`. A High compatibility risk remains: shared FK-check locks can’t be upgraded to exclusive later in the same txn, so enabling the sysvar can make later DML on the referenced rows fail.
